Counsel for Opposite Party :- Anuruddh Chaturvedi,Dinesh Kumar Sharma,G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri G.S. Chaturvedi, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Vishal Kashyap, learned counsel
for the applicant and Sri Anuruddh Chaturvedi, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri
Sunil Kumar, learned Aga for the State.

2.  The present anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case No.
7991 of 2023, arising out of F.I.R./Case Crime No. 376 of 2023, under Section 304 of IPC, Police Station - Khurja Nagar, District - Bulandshahr, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the applicant, who happens to be a medical practitioner, is stated to have treated the son of the informant Ashwani Gaur, who was a student of B.A. L.L.B. Ist year and was suffering from fever since last 4-5 days.
On 11.02.2023, the informant along with his wife took his son to the clinic of the applicant for treatment.
The applicant is stated to have advised several blood tests to his son and only minor urine infection was found in the report.

The informant again went to the applicant on 13.02.2023 whereby he was advised to get an ultrasound examination of his son and after seeing the report of ultrasound, the applicant is stated to have advised the informant to admit his son at his hospital and was given treatment there.
Other members of the family of the informant were also present there.
4. The applicant is stated to have administered five injections to his blood vessels directly.
The wife of the informant told the applicant that her son has not eaten anything today, as such, he should not give him injections.

On seeing the condition of the son of the informant worsening, the applicant is stated to have advised him to take his son to Kailash Hospital at Khurja and the applicant himself took him to the said hospital and got him admitted in ICU.
The applicant and his manager Prem Prakash Arora were also present at the hospital for about one and a half hour.
Thereafter, the applicant is stated to have told the informant and his family members that the condition of his son is stable and he shall visit the hospital again at 05:00 PM.
The applicant was heard by the informant and his family members saying that he has mistakenly administered the injections at one time instead of giving the same with a gap of 12 hours.
The informant and his family members were not allowed to enter the ICU and see the condition of their ailing son.

The wife of the informant went inside and saw her son gasping and was told by the consultant Anaesthetist doctor Rana Chaudhary that condition of her son was critical and he may be put on ventilatory support.
On being questioned by her, doctor is stated to have lost his temper and asked her to take her son to any other place.
The ambulance was not provided to the informant by the manager, Prem Prakash Arora and he deliberately delayed it

, as such, the informant himself arranged the ambulance from Bulandshahr and took his son at about 07:00 PM to Kailash Hospital, Noida where seeing his critical condition,
he was put on ventilatory support and subsequently, he expired there on 14.02.2023.
It is also alleged in the FIR that the son of the informant has expired due to the wrong treatment deliberately given by the applicant and other co-accused persons.

RIVAL CONTENTIONS:
Arguments on behalf of the applicant:
5. Learned Senior Counsel for the applicant has stated that admittedly, the applicant is the family friend of the informant and has acted bonafidely with extra care and had himself taken the son of informant to the hospital for better treatment.
It is further submitted that no offence u/s 304 IPC is made out against the applicant or any other accused persons.
The applicant has given the treatment to his son at initial stage only.
6. It is argued that the informant had filed an application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. on 27.02.2023 before the C.J.M. Bulandshahr against the applicant.

He had again moved an application u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C.
before the C.J.M. Bulandshahr on 17.03.2023 thereby implicating another person i.e. Prem Prakash Dr Neeraj Kumar vs State Of Up And Another on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4740208/
2 Arora also, who happens to be the administrative manager of Kailash Hospital, Khurja.

sentences.text: On 20.03.2023, C.J.M. Bulandshahr directed the C.M.O., Bulandshahr to set up a medical board regarding the matter in hand and to submit the report of the same before the court.

On 25.03.2023,
C.M.O., Bulandshahr formed a medical board consisting of five doctors of PMHS.

The medical board constituted by the C.M.O. submitted a report after due enquiry and after recording the statements of all the doctors who treated the deceased and found that the treatment given to his son Ashwani Gaur from 11.02.2023 to 14.02.2023 was proper as normally such patients are treated in the said manner only.
The medical board expressed inability to give any opinion on the delay in providing the ambulance, if any, to the informant.

7. It is further argued that despite the said report of the Board concerned, learned C.J.M. allowed the application of the informant in a mechanical way vide order dated 10.05.2023 and ordered for institution of FIR against the applicant and co-accused Prem Prakash Arora.
The instant FIR was registered on 12.05.2023.

The applicant challenged the registering of the said FIR by filing a Writ Petition No.8295 of 2023 and this Court was pleased to grant protection to the applicant against arrest till submission of final report (charge-sheet) vide order dated 30.05.2023.
8.
The investigating agency submitted the final report (charge-sheet) against the applicant u/s 304 IPC on 25.08.2023.
Subsequently, summons were issued against him.
The applicant had challenged the said final report by preferring a petition u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No.39316 of 2023 and the same was dismissed by this Court vide order dated 27.10.2023.
The applicant challenged the said rejection order dated 27.10.2023 before the Supreme Court and the matter was remanded back vide order dated 24.11.2023.
The applicant moved a recall application before this Court and the said recall application was also rejected vide order dated 04.04.2024.
It is also argued that the instant case at the most may fall under Section 304-A of IPC, as the applicant in a bonafide act, had treated his son.

He has no criminal history to his credit.
9.
It is also submitted that the rigors of judgement of this Court passed in Shivam Vs. State of U.P.

and Another1, does not apply to the instant case as the applicant who is a medical practitioner, has been falsely implicated by the informant in the present case peeved by the sad demise of his son out of vengeance.

10. It is further stated that the FIR is delayed and even the application to the S.S.P., Bulandshahr was moved on 22.02.2023 which is also delayed by about six days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

11. Learned Senior Counsel has further stated that in the present case, there is no need of custodial interrogation as the applicant is a reputed citizen of the locality and in the light of the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Aman Preet Singh vs. C.B.I. through Director2, wherein the Court has clearly held that if a person, who is an accused in a non-bailable/cognizable offence, was not taken into custody during the period of investigation, in such a case, it is appropriate that he may be released on bail as the circumstances of his having not been arrested during investigation or not being produced in custody is itself sufficient to entitle him to be released on bail.

It is also argued that the medical professionals, who when found to have taken reasonable care and caution cannot Dr Neeraj Kumar vs State Of Up And Another on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4740208/
3 be exposed to criminal prosecution.
12. Much reliance has been placed on the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Jacob Mathew Vs.
State of Punjab3, whereby the prosecution of the accused in the said case was quashed and the term "negligence" was defined in detail.

entities.text:
Jacob Mathew Vs.
State of Punjab3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, Supreme Court has held that a private complaint may not be entertained unless the complainant has produced prima facie evidence before the court in the form of a credible opinion given by another competent doctor to support the charges of rashness or negligence on the part of the accused doctor.

The investigating officer should before proceeding against the doctor accused of rashness or negligent act or omission, obtain an independent and complete medical opinion preferably from a doctor in government service qualified in that branch of medical practice who can normally be expected to have an impartial and unbiased opinion applying Bolam's test to the facts collected in the investigation.
A doctor accused of rashness or negligence may not be arrested in a routine manner simply because a charge has been levelled against him.
Herein the report of the board set up by the CMO proves that applicant had provided treatment as per standard protocols.

13. Learned Senior Counsel has also placed reliance of the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Martin F. D'Souza Vs. Mohd. Ishfaq4, wherein it has been held as under:-
"We, therefore, direct that whenever a complaint is received against a doctor or hospital by the Consumer Fora (whether District, State or National) or by the Criminal Court then before issuing notice to the doctor or hospital against whom the complaint was made the Consumer Forum or Criminal Court should first refer the matter to a competent doctor or committee of doctors, specialized in the field relating to which the medical negligence is attributed, and only after that doctor or committee reports that there is a prima facie case of medical negligence should notice be then issued to the concerned doctor/hospital.

entities.text: Martin F. D'Souza Vs. Mohd. Ishfaq4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This is necessary to avoid harassment to doctors who may not be ultimately found to be negligent.

We further warn the police officials not to arrest or harass doctors unless the facts clearly come within the parameters laid down in Jacob Mathew's case (supra), otherwise the policemen will themselves have to face legal action."
14. Under such circumstances, the applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail.

Arguments on behalf of the informant:
15.
It is argued that the applicant was the doctor who was responsible for the death of the son of the informant as he has acted in a very negligent and lethargic way.
His misconduct is evident from the circumstances of the death of his son.

The applicant was asked certain questions by the Investigating Officer and he has categorically stated in it that he had given injection FALSIGO 60 MG as he had seen one episode of rigors and vomiting.

On being asked by the Investigating Officer as to whether he had given any antidote to the patient after his deteriorating condition, the answer was in affirmative but he had stated that he had not mentioned the details of the said antidote in the description of the treatment.

The applicant did not give any discharge summary to the informant Dr Neeraj Kumar vs State Of Up And Another on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4740208/
4 and several questions were asked regarding the reactions and contra-indications of certain medicines on the patient.
16.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel has placed much reliance on the judgement of this Court passed in Shivam Vs.
State of U.P. and Another, reported in AIROnline 2021 All 484, and has stated that the applicant was not entitled for anticipatory bail as he has agitated the provisions of Section 482 Cr.P.C. and failed, as such, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

entities.text:
Shivam Vs.
State of U.P. and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Paragraph 43(8) of the aforesaid judgement states that the anticipatory bail cannot be granted to an accused after submission of charge sheet.

The relevant para-43(8) of the judgement reads as under:-
"(8) Where the accused has unsuccessfully challenged the charge-sheet before this Court or any proceedings are pending before this Court regarding the charge sheet submitted against the accused;"
17. Learned AGA has also opposed the anticipatory bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant is not cooperating in trial.
Although he was not arrested during investigation but his statement was taken by the Investigating Officer.
However, learned AGA could not dispute the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.

CONCLUSION:
18. Relying on its judgement passed in Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar5, the Supreme Court in Md.
Asfak Alam Vs. State of Jharkhand and another6, has stated that once the charge-sheet was filed and there was no impediment, at least on the part of the accused, the court having regard to the nature of the offences, the allegations and the maximum sentence of the offences they were likely to carry, ought to have granted the bail as a matter of course.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Asfak Alam Vs. State of Jharkhand and another6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the court did not do so but mechanically rejected and, virtually, to rub salt in the wound directed the appellant to surrender and seek regular bail before the trial court.
Thus, the High Court fell into error in adopting such a casual approach.

19. The judgement of Shivam (supra) cannot be applied to the instant case as the applicant is a medical practitioner and as per the report of medical board constituted by CMO, the applicant had treated the patient in proper manner.
The pious relationship between the doctor and the patient is at stake in the instant case.

20. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the medical board set up by the CMO has exonerated the applicant in his report coupled by the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and also considering the judgements of Shivam (supra), Aman Preet Singh (supra),
Jacob Mathew (supra), Martin F. D'Souza (supra), Arnesh Kumar (supra) and Md. Asfak Alam (supra), I find it a fit case to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail.
21. Without expressing any opinion upon ultimate merits of the case either ways which may adversely affect the trial of the case, the anticipatory bail application of the applicant is allowed.

24. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
